html:
Hurricane Dorian struck the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama on 1 September 2019 as a category 5 storm, then stalled over Grand Bahama for more than a day. It is the worst natural disaster in the history of the Bahamas.

Winds near 300 km/h and a huge storm surge flattened whole districts. Many of the dead lived in shanty towns of Haitian migrants in Marsh Harbour. Dozens were confirmed dead and many more were never found.

Damage came to billions of dollars, a large share of the country's economy. The storm, like Irma and Maria two years before, fed debate about stronger storms in a warming climate.
sum: Hurricane Dorian struck the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama on 1 September 2019 as a category 5 storm, then stalled over Grand Bahama for more than a day. It is the worst natural disaster in the history of the Bahamas.
